accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes insurance density from insurance penetration?
o: Insurance density is total premium as a percentage of GDP, whereas insurance penetration is premium per capita
Insurance density refers to claims settled, whereas insurance penetration refers to policies issued
Insurance density is premium per capita, whereas insurance penetration is total premium as a percentage of GDP
Both terms refer to the number of insured persons per 1,000 population
accepted.x: Insurance density is measured as premium per capita, generally in US dollars. Insurance penetration is the total premium as a percentage of GDP; neither measure means insured persons per 100 or 1,000 people.
accepted.tq: Separate the two look-alike terms by matching each with its precise denominator.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The recommendation to open the insurance sector to private companies and create an independent regulator was made by which committee?
accepted.x: The Malhotra Committee, constituted in 1993–94, recommended opening insurance to private companies and establishing an independent regulator.
accepted.tq: Use the committee-to-recommendation association rather than a broad sectoral guess.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reform of the insurance sector:
1. The IRDA Act was enacted in 1999.
2. The IRDA Act opened the insurance sector to private companies.
3. The reform created a statutory insurance regulator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IRDA Act, 1999 opened the insurance sector to private participation and established the statutory Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.
accepted.tq: Check whether the date, reform measure and institutional consequence belong to the same legislation.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India is headquartered at:
accepted.x: IRDAI is a statutory body headquartered in Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Test the headquarters-location association while avoiding the common capital-city substitution.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the origin of LIC is correct?
o: LIC was formed in 1972 under the General Insurance Business Act.
LIC was established in 1999 under the IRDA Act.
LIC was formed on 1 September 1956 under the LIC Act, 1956, by nationalising life insurers.
LIC was formed in 1948 by nationalising general insurers.
accepted.x: LIC was formed on 1 September 1956 under the LIC Act, 1956, through the nationalisation of life insurers.
accepted.tq: Combine the institution, date, enabling Act and nature of nationalisation.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: General insurance business in India was nationalised under which institution in 1972?
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
accepted.x: General insurance was nationalised under the General Insurance Corporation in 1972, whereas life insurance had been nationalised through LIC in 1956.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two nationalisation episodes by sector and institution.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the insurance-law amendment of 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It raised the foreign direct investment cap in insurance to 100 per cent.
2. It amended the Insurance Act, 1938, the LIC Act, 1956 and the IRDA Act, 1999.
3. It created a Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2025 amendment raised the FDI cap from 74 per cent to 100 per cent, amended the three specified Acts and created the Policyholders' Education and Protection Fund.
accepted.tq: Verify each legal consequence separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025 was passed by Parliament on:
accepted.x: Parliament passed the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act on 17 December 2025; it was notified in late December 2025.
accepted.tq: Use the exact date and distinguish passage from later notification.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the 2025 insurance-law amendment, the net-owned fund requirement for foreign reinsurers was reduced from:
accepted.x: The amendment reduced the net-owned fund requirement for foreign reinsurers from Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 1,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Compare the original and revised thresholds rather than recalling only one figure.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: “Insurance for All by 2047” is the vision of:
o: The Life Insurance Corporation of India
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India
accepted.x: “Insurance for All by 2047” is the vision articulated by IRDAI.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution associated with the exact policy vision.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding recent insurance-sector developments?
o: The FDI cap was reduced from 100 per cent to 74 per cent in 2025.
Premium income was Rs 11.9 lakh crore in FY25 and health overtook motor as the leading non-life business.
Life and individual health policies became subject to GST from September 2025.
Motor insurance has overtaken health insurance as the leading non-life business.
accepted.x: Insurance premium income was Rs 11.9 lakh crore in FY25, and health insurance overtook motor insurance as the leading non-life business. Life and individual health policies became GST-exempt from September 2025.
accepted.tq: Reject reversed trends and tax-status substitutions using the precise policy wording.
accepted.sec: Insurance - penetration vs density, IRDAI, private entry, LIC, FDI cap, Insurance for All by 2047  [APPSC]

accepted.s: NIDHI, in the tourism sector, refers to:
o: National Information Database for Domestic Holidays in India
National Initiative for Domestic Heritage Infrastructure
National Index for Development of Heritage Institutions
National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry
accepted.x: NIDHI stands for National Integrated Database of Hospitality Industry and is a technology-driven database of hospitality and accommodation units maintained by the Ministry of Tourism.
accepted.tq: Expand the acronym and connect it with the responsible ministry and database function.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly describes Swadesh Darshan and Swadesh Darshan 2.0?
1. Swadesh Darshan was launched in 2014–15 as a theme-based tourist-circuit scheme.
2. Swadesh Darshan 2.0 focuses on sustainable and responsible destinations.
3. Swadesh Darshan was designed exclusively for pilgrimage-site development.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect because the exclusive development of pilgrimage sites is associated with PRASHAD, not Swadesh Darshan.
accepted.tq: Separate two neighbouring tourism schemes by launch period, thematic focus and target destination.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PRASHAD is primarily concerned with:
accepted.x: PRASHAD stands for Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive and is intended for developing pilgrimage sites.
accepted.tq: Use the scheme’s expanded form to identify its functional domain.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PRASHAD was launched in which period?
accepted.x: PRASHAD was launched in 2014–15.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its exact launch period and avoid confusing it with later tourism initiatives.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index was published by the:
accepted.x: The Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index was published by the World Economic Forum.
accepted.tq: Apply the world-body attribution trap by distinguishing the publisher from other international institutions.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index has been renamed the:
accepted.x: The Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index was renamed the Travel and Tourism Development Index.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the former title from the current official name.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about tourism in India in FY24:
1. Travel and tourism accounted for 5.22 per cent of GDP.
2. The sector employed about 13.3 per cent of the workforce.
3. Tourism’s share of GDP was stated to be 13.3 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Travel and tourism accounted for 5.22 per cent of GDP and employed about 13.3 per cent of the workforce. Statement 3 wrongly transfers the workforce figure to GDP share.
accepted.tq: Catch the reversed-comparison trap by assigning each percentage to its correct indicator.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following was identified as a sustainable-tourism measure?
1. Development of long-distance hiking trails
2. A Marina Development Policy
3. Replacement of all domestic tourism by international tourism
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Long-distance hiking trails and a Marina Development Policy were identified as sustainable-tourism measures. Replacing domestic tourism with international tourism is not such a measure.
accepted.tq: Find the one policy statement that is inconsistent with the sustainability objective.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In 2024, which of the following trends was reported for domestic and international visitors to India?
o: Domestic visitors rose but international visitors declined.
International visitors rose but domestic visitors declined.
Both domestic and international visitors rose.
Both domestic and international visitors declined.
accepted.x: Both domestic and international visitors increased in 2024.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of two related trends without introducing unsupported numerical totals.
accepted.sec: Tourism - NIDHI, Swadesh Darshan, PRASHAD, tourist visits, TTCI, sustainable tourism  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the National Health Accounts data, government health spending as a percentage of GDP in 2018–19 was:
accepted.x: Government public-health spending was 1.28 per cent of GDP in 2018–19.
accepted.tq: Match the percentage with the correct NHA year rather than with the later target or estimate.
accepted.sec: Health services - public health expenditure (NHA), Centre + states spending  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The latest government health expenditure figure cited in relation to GDP was:
o: 1.43 per cent, against an NHP 2017 target of 2.5 per cent
4.89 per cent, against an NHP 2017 target of 6.12 per cent
2.5 per cent, against an NHP 2017 target of 1.43 per cent
1.28 per cent, against an NHP target of 1.43 per cent
accepted.x: The latest cited government health expenditure was 1.43 per cent of GDP, below the National Health Policy 2017 target of 2.5 per cent.
accepted.tq: Compare the actual expenditure figure with the policy target and reject reversed values.
accepted.sec: Health services - public health expenditure (NHA), Centre + states spending  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The share of health in total government expenditure, including the Centre and States, changed from 6.12 per cent in 2021–22 to which level in 2022–23?
accepted.x: Health’s share of total government expenditure fell from 6.12 per cent in 2021–22 to 4.89 per cent in 2022–23. It was 5.02 per cent in 2019–20.
accepted.tq: Read the direction and endpoint of a three-year percentage comparison carefully.
accepted.sec: Health services - public health expenditure (NHA), Centre + states spending  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the coverage and utilisation figures associated with PM-JAY and State schemes?
o: They cover about 70 per cent of citizens, of whom about 35 per cent used the benefit.
They cover about 80 per cent of citizens, of whom about 35 per cent used the benefit.
They cover about 35 per cent of citizens, of whom about 80 per cent used the benefit.
They cover about 80 per cent of citizens, and all beneficiaries used the benefit.
accepted.x: PM-JAY and State schemes together cover about 80 per cent of citizens, but only about 35 per cent of those insured used the benefit.
accepted.tq: Keep coverage and utilisation as separate measures instead of reversing their percentages.
accepted.sec: Health services - public health expenditure (NHA), Centre + states spending  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to PM-JAY, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2018.
2. It provides coverage of Rs 5 lakh per family.
3. Insurance coverage has roughly tripled since its beginning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: PM-JAY was launched in 2018 with coverage of Rs 5 lakh per family, and insurance coverage has roughly tripled since its launch.
accepted.tq: Combine the scheme’s launch year, benefit amount and reported outcome in one coded question.
accepted.sec: Health services - public health expenditure (NHA), Centre + states spending  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, banks may undertake para-banking activities:
o: Only after approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India
With the approval of the Reserve Bank of India
Only when authorised by the State Government
accepted.x: Section 6 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 permits banks to undertake specified para-banking activities with RBI approval.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority would approve the banking activity rather than confusing regulators.
accepted.sec: Para-banking services - activities permitted to banks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a permitted para-banking activity of banks under the stated framework?
accepted.x: Portfolio management and investment advisory, primary dealership and pension fund management are among the permitted para-banking activities. Conducting legislative elections is not a banking activity.
accepted.tq: Identify the outsider in a list of closely related financial activities.
accepted.sec: Para-banking services - activities permitted to banks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A bank proposes to enter into an arrangement to distribute insurance products. Which form is specifically permitted under the para-banking framework?
o: Only as an unregulated informal intermediary
As a corporate agent or through a joint venture
Only through a State-owned insurance corporation
Only after converting into a non-banking financial company
accepted.x: Banks may undertake insurance business as a corporate agent or through a joint venture, subject to the applicable regulatory approval.
accepted.tq: Apply the permitted institutional forms to a practical banking situation.
accepted.sec: Para-banking services - activities permitted to banks  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

A. Equipment leasing — Para-banking activity
B. Factoring — Para-banking activity
C. Mutual funds — Para-banking activity
D. All the above
accepted.x: Equipment leasing, factoring and mutual-fund business are all among the para-banking activities that banks may undertake with RBI approval.
accepted.tq: Recognise that all three financial-service activities belong to the permitted category.
accepted.sec: Para-banking services - activities permitted to banks  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rajiv Aarogyasri was initially launched in united Andhra Pradesh as a scheme for:
o: Free higher education for economically weaker students
Cashless health insurance for families below the poverty line
Universal pension support for senior citizens
accepted.x: Rajiv Aarogyasri was launched as a cashless health insurance scheme for families below the poverty line and operated through a State trust.
accepted.tq: Identify the scheme’s target group and benefit type rather than relying only on its name.
accepted.sec: AP health scheme Aarogyasri - launch, eponym, coverage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rajiv Aarogyasri was operated through a:
accepted.x: The scheme was run through a State trust.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional delivery mechanism associated with the health scheme.
accepted.sec: AP health scheme Aarogyasri - launch, eponym, coverage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the initial launch of Aarogyasri is correct?
o: It was launched on 17 December 2025 by the IRDAI.
It was launched in 2018 by the Union Government under PM-JAY.
It was launched on 1 September 1956 by the Government of India.
It was launched on 1 April 2007 by the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government in united Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: Rajiv Aarogyasri was launched on 1 April 2007 in united Andhra Pradesh by the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government.
accepted.tq: Combine the exact date, jurisdiction and launching government while rejecting swapped schemes and institutions.
accepted.sec: AP health scheme Aarogyasri - launch, eponym, coverage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The name “Rajiv Aarogyasri” was given in honour of:
accepted.x: The scheme was named after Rajiv Gandhi; it was launched by the Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy government.
accepted.tq: Separate the person after whom a scheme is named from the government that launched it.
accepted.sec: AP health scheme Aarogyasri - launch, eponym, coverage  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the cited 2026 reference, State and Central health-insurance schemes together covered approximately what share of Andhra Pradesh households?
accepted.x: State and Central health-insurance schemes together covered approximately 70 per cent of households in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Andhra Pradesh household figure from the wider citizen-coverage figure under PM-JAY and State schemes.
accepted.sec: AP health scheme Aarogyasri - launch, eponym, coverage  [APPSC]
